Context: UpdateCommandForCurrentBinary feeds both maybeAutoUpdate (which says "run the following in PowerShell") and checkpointpolicy.UnsupportedPolicyMessage (cmd/entire/cli/checkpointpolicy/policy.go:87, "Upgrade Entire, then rerun the command: <cmd>"), which names no shell. Before this branch the Windows unknown-location value was the releases URL, which pasted anywhere; the Scoop migration command in versioncheck_windows.go is wrapped in `cmd.exe /D /C` for that same paste-anywhere reason. Under Git Bash a hook prints `iex "& {$(irm https://entire.io/install.ps1)} -InstallDir '...' -NoPathUpdate"`, and pasting it into bash expands `$(irm ...)` before PowerShell ever runs; in cmd.exe `iex` is not a command.

Pick one and apply it consistently (my recommendation is the first, it is smaller and keeps the README shape):
1. Have UnsupportedPolicyMessage's Windows output say the command runs in PowerShell, mirroring the maybeAutoUpdate hint. That likely means a per-OS hint string or letting the caller pass it; keep it out of the cobra Long text.
2. Wrap the fallback as `powershell -NoProfile -Command "..."` so every Windows command pastes into cmd, PowerShell, and Git Bash like the Scoop one. Mind the nested quoting of the -InstallDir literal (quoteInsideDoubleQuoted) and update the pinned strings in versioncheck_windows_test.go and autoupdate_windows_test.go.

Files: cmd/entire/cli/versioncheck/versioncheck_windows.go (fallbackInstallCommand, lines 126-139), cmd/entire/cli/versioncheck/autoupdate.go, cmd/entire/cli/checkpointpolicy/policy.go and its tests. Verify with `GOOS=windows go vet ./cmd/entire/cli/versioncheck/ && GOOS=windows go test -c -o /dev/null ./cmd/entire/cli/versioncheck/`, `go test ./cmd/entire/cli/versioncheck/ ./cmd/entire/cli/checkpointpolicy/`, and lint via ~/.local/share/mise/installs/golangci-lint/2.11.3/golangci-lint-2.11.3-darwin-arm64/golangci-lint (the `mise run lint` shim is a stale v1). When done, resolve the finding with `entire trail finding resolve 01M1XKACB96XNW5RY20FZ8S1QH --trail 1201` and reply to me (uninstall-ext-ps1-autoupdate-ac). There is one more finding after this; I will send it once you report back.

git add -A && git commit -q -F - <<'MSG' && git log --oneline -1
Name PowerShell in the checkpoint-policy upgrade hint

The Windows update command is a PowerShell one-liner. maybeAutoUpdate said
so ("run the following in PowerShell"); UnsupportedPolicyMessage printed the
same command under "Upgrade Entire, then rerun the command" and named no
shell. In cmd.exe `iex` is not a command, and pasting the -InstallDir form
into Git Bash expands `$(irm ...)` before PowerShell ever runs.

versioncheck.UpdateCommandShell reports the shell its command needs —
PowerShell on Windows, "" on unix, where brew/mise/curl|bash run anywhere —
and travels with the command into the message.
